sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Growth stepped up to 17.5% and 18.0% in FY2021 and FY2022, fell to 6.9% in FY2023, then recovered to 17.8% in FY2026 [D205][D258][D311][D472].
The FY2026 rebound was driven by Microsoft Cloud, with Intelligent Cloud revenue rising on Azure [P17].
Operating margin climbed from 30.1% to 46.8% over the window, a 16.7pp gain, and net income compounded at 20.2% against revenue's 14.7% [F41][F50][F224][F221].
Microsoft Cloud reached $214.4 billion, or 64.6% of revenue, in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% growth [S24][D566][D568][D472].
Server products and cloud services revenue rose 31% on Azure and other cloud services, which grew 41% [P12].
That product line contributed 11.0pp of growth and was 39.0% of revenue, the largest single driver [D642][D640].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 [D649][P14].
Operating income grew 20.8% against revenue's 17.8%, an incremental margin of 53.3%, while operating expenses rose only 7.4% [D473][D472][D498][D491].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the FY2017 low [F50][D975][F41].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as cost of revenue grew 21.1% and took 0.9pp off operating margin [F30][D981][D489][D500].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
R&D fell to 10.7% of revenue, a window low, and added 0.8pp to margin, while selling and marketing fell to 8.0% [D985][D501][D451].
Net margin of 40.3% sat 6.5pp below operating margin, versus 9.5pp in FY2025, as other income swung to a $10.7 billion gain on OpenAI dilution [F70][D1023][D1022][X124][P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion, or 55.1% of revenue, while free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion [F100][D477][D457][F120][D478].
Operating cash rose on higher customer receipts and lower income taxes paid, offset by more paid to suppliers [P1].
Capex of $115.9 billion was 34.9% of revenue and 3.38x D&A, leaving free cash flow at 0.50x net income, a window low against a 0.91x median [F110][D455][D461][D460][D990].
Investing outflow rose $66.9 billion, mainly a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions [P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, or 22.0% of revenue, with total debt down 6.6% to $40.3 billion [D465][D466][D464][D495].
That net cash ratio sits in the 83rd percentile of six software peers, whose median is -7.2% [D1006][D1007].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion were 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
The diluted share count fell only 0.2%, so EPS growth of 31.6% came almost entirely from net income growth of 31.3% [D493][D476][D474].
Free cash flow fell below 80% of net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at 0.70x and 0.50x, as capex outran cash generation [R1][D406][D460].
This is the clearest deterioration in the pack: free cash flow margin of 20.2% is a window low and sits in the 20th percentile of five peers against a 34.7% median [D982][D1002][D1003].
FY2017 short-term investments were not reported, so cash and investments and net cash omit them for that year [R6][X158].
That liquidity break makes any net cash comparison spanning FY2017 unreliable, though it does not affect the latest-year figures.
If capex stays above the FY2026 level of 34.9% of revenue, free cash flow margin would likely remain below its 30.3% median [D455][D984].
A gross margin recovery above the 68.2% median would signal AI infrastructure costs are being absorbed [D981].
Operating margin holding above the 46.8% high would confirm the operating leverage of FY2026, when expenses grew 7.4% against revenue's 17.8% [F50][D491][D472].
